text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London reversed earlier downward direction to finish slightly higher but still failed to catch up with a rebound in New York. While supplies in the arabica sector are extremely tight, the robusta market is well supplied. Robustas are now trading at an unprecedented $1.40/lb below arabica prices and traders expect the huge gap to remain for some time. Robusta prices are weaker not only because of more ample supplies but also because of changes in grading terms making it a risky proposition to take delivery of May if there is any thought of putting it back on the board in July when the changes come into effect.

May added $4.00 to close at $1,632 per tonne, while July closed $7.00 higher at $1,662 per tonne. Arabica futures in New York closed sharply higher due to tight supplies and news that negotiations aimed at resolving a truckers' strike in Colombia had reached a stalemate. The recent round of speculative profit-taking has apparently run its course and traders said that it is only a matter of time before the 224 cents/lb level is surpassed. They said that with arabica inventories already near historically low levels in the U.S., a prolonged work stoppage in Colombia could drive futures prices to new highs. May added 3.10 cents/lb to close at 214.30 cents/lb, while July closed 5.05 cents/lb higher at 193.40 cents/lb. The outer months gained between 4.45 to 0.25 cents/lb.

EL SALVADOR - According to the Salvadoran Coffee Council, coffee production in 1997/98 (October/September) could be around 2.45 million 60-kg bags, 7 percent larger than the 1996/97 crop. However, the 1996/97 figure seems to be fairly low given the country's export performance in the first few months. Moreover, it is very early to give a precise estimate for 1997/98.
UNITED STATES - U.S. certified coffee stocks showed another decline on April 22 with the total at 56,600 bags, down from 60,349 bags on April 21. There were 500 bags pending grading in New York.

SOUTH KOREA - South Korea imported 915,400 bags of coffee in January/November 1996, 7 percent less than in the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 7.5 percent to 1.084 million bags. Main suppliers of green coffee in January/November 1996 were Honduras (125,500 vs 97,000 bags), Colombia (114,600 vs 124,100 bags), Indonesia (209,500 vs 64,600 bags) and Thailand (101,600 vs 156,400 bags).

TANZANIA - Tanzania exported 323,900 bags of coffee in July/December 1996, down from 339,100 bags in the same period in 1995. Total exports in crop year 1995/96 (July/June) reached 934,800 bags. The main country of destination for Tanzanian coffee in July/December 1996 remained Germany (109,000 vs 109,300 bags), followed by Japan (52,900 vs 49,800 bags). Another major buyer of coffee from Tanzania were the Netherlands (49,400 vs 37,500 bags).
